newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: HINDMARSH BRIDGE IMPORTANT HIGH COURT TEST CASE: OPPOSITION
The Federal Opposition says an expected High Court challenge to the Hindmarsh Island bridge by Aborigines in South Australia would be an important test case.
The Ngarrindjeri people who are opposed to the project say they'll lodge a challenge to the Senate's go-ahead in the High Court.
Opposition Aboriginal affairs spokesman Daryl Melham says taking the case to the High Court would take the politics out of it.
Mr Melham says the outcome also has ramifications for the Wik legislation.
He says there's a strong argument the sole purpose of both the Hindmarsh legislation and the Wik legislation is to discriminate against Aborigines, which is an abuse of the Constitution.

COMMITTEE SAYS THIRD FORCE IN AUSTRALIAN MEDIA MAY BE NEEDED The Chair of the Federal Government's Communications committee says for diversity and competition reasons, it might be in Australia's interests to have an overseas buyer purchase Fairfax.
The committee's scheduled to meet Communications Minister Richard Alston tomorrow for further discussions about the review of cross-media ownership laws.
Committee Chair, Paul Neville, told ABC radio that some judicious overseas ownership would be preferable to Australia's core media facilities being held by only two players.
He says several committee members share his view.
EMMA GEORGE RECORDS RATIFIED BY IAAF
Three world pole vault records set by Australia's Emma George have finally been ratified by the International Amateur Athletics Federation.
The two indoor records of 4-point-3 and 4-point-four metres were set in December, the outdoor record of 4-point-five metres was set in February.
After what she described as a poor performance in Japan at the weekend, George is looking forward to Europe's summer athletics season which starets next month.
